# Map Reading Lab: caption rehearsal

**Event:** November 12, 2026, at 14:00 UTC, in `room-map`.

The presenter and room host rehearse captions at **13:50 UTC** on the event date. Use the card for your assignment: [presenter](#presenter-card) or [host](#host-card). The presenter supplies the spoken test; the host checks what the room's caption system produces.

## Presenter card

Join `room-map` in Forum Live 1.8 at **13:50 UTC on November 12, 2026**, for the Map Reading Lab caption rehearsal. The live session begins at 14:00 UTC. You provide microphone audio for this test; the host handles the room's caption controls.

The caption language is **English (United States)**. Speak in that language during the rehearsal and session so the host can test the caption configuration that the workshop will use.

> Captions use microphone audio, not screen-shared slide text. Read an important place name aloud instead of relying on the audience seeing its written form on a slide.

1. Join the rehearsal with your microphone ready to use.
2. Say the test sentence: **North is at the top.**
3. Pause while the host compares the displayed caption line with the sentence. Continue the rehearsal only after the host confirms a match.
4. If the host reports a missing or incorrect word, repeat the sentence into the microphone so the host can check the new line.

## Host card

Join `room-map` in Forum Live 1.8 at **13:50 UTC on November 12, 2026**, for the Map Reading Lab caption rehearsal. You are responsible for setting up caption generation and confirming the test before the live session at 14:00 UTC.

> Captions use microphone audio, not screen-shared slide text. A visible sentence on a shared slide is not a substitute for the presenter's spoken test.

1. Open **Room > Captions**. Select **English (United States)** and choose **Start captions**. This starts caption generation for the room.
2. Open **View > Captions** to display the generated captions on your own screen. This is a personal display control, separate from the room-wide generation control.
3. Ask the presenter to say **North is at the top.** Compare the displayed caption line with that exact sentence.
4. If a word is wrong or absent, ask the presenter to repeat the sentence using microphone audio. Compare the new line before confirming the test. Send an unconfirmed test to the event coordinator before the live session.
5. Leave room-wide caption generation on for the **14:00 UTC** session.

Participants can use **View > Captions** to show captions on their own screens. You can turn off your personal caption display without stopping room-wide generation; do not confuse hiding your display with ending captions for the room.
